Prealgebra · Lesson 6.4

Turning Words into Equations

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A word problem states a fact in words. Your job is to write that same fact as an equation. The sentence a number tripled and then reduced by four gives eleven becomes 3x−4=113x−4=11. Five steps handle every problem of this kind. Read the whole problem, name the unknown with a letter, translate each phrase by its meaning, solve, then answer the exact question asked and check it against the original story.

Problem
An arcade prize machine doubles the bronze tokens you feed it and drops in 77 bonus tokens, and after Priya's turn the screen reads 3131. In other words, seven more than twice her tokens is thirty-one. How many bronze tokens did Priya feed the machine?
Show a hint
  • Give the unknown a name first. Let xx be the number of tokens Priya fed the machine. Now translate the sentence one phrase at a time. What does "twice her tokens" become, and what does "seven more than" that become? The words "is thirty-one" hand you the equals sign.
  • Twice her tokens is 2x2x, and seven more than that is 2x+72x+7. The phrase "is thirty-one" sets it equal to 3131, so your equation is 2x+7=312x+7=31. Subtract 77 from both sides, then divide by 22.
Show the full solution
Let xx be the tokens Priya fed in. Twice her tokens plus seven is thirty-one, so 2x+7=312x+7=31. Subtract 77 to get 2x=242x=24, then divide by 22, so she fed in 1212​ tokens. Translate one phrase at a time. Twice gives 2x2x, seven more than adds 77, and is hands you the equals sign.
Problem
A beekeeper scoops out exactly a third of whatever a jar holds, pours it into a bottle, then stirs in 99 more ounces. The bottle then weighs 1717 ounces, since here the word of means multiply. How many ounces of honey did the jar hold at the start?
Show a hint
  • Let xx stand for the number of ounces the jar held at the start. Now read the words one piece at a time and turn each piece into math. "A third of the amount" becomes 13x31​x, "increased by nine" adds 99, and "is seventeen" gives you the equals sign and the 1717.
  • Your equation is 13x+9=1731​x+9=17. Subtract 99 from both sides to get 13x=831​x=8, then multiply both sides by 33 to undo the one third.
Show the full solution
Let xx be the ounces the jar held at the start. A third of that plus nine ounces is seventeen, so 13x+9=1731​x+9=17. Subtract 99 to get 13x=831​x=8, then multiply both sides by 33, so the jar held 2424​ ounces. Check it. A third of 2424 is 88, and nine more is 1717.
Problem
Maya tapes streamers to a wall, and the number on the wall is nineteen fewer than the number in her box, which counts out to 4040. Watch the order. Fewer than subtracts from the number, so this is x−19x−19, not 19−x19−x. How many streamers were in Maya's box to start with?
Show a hint
  • Let xx be the number of streamers in the box. The phrase "nineteen fewer than the number" means you start with the number and take 19 away, so it becomes x−19x−19, not 19−x19−x. Set that equal to 40.
  • Solve x−19=40x−19=40 by adding 19 to both sides. Then read your answer back into the words to make sure nineteen fewer really lands on forty.
Show the full solution
Let xx be the streamers in Maya's box. Nineteen fewer than that number is x−19x−19, and it equals forty, so x−19=40x−19=40. Add 1919 to both sides, so the box held 5959​ streamers. Fewer than reverses the order you hear it in. Reading it as 19−x19−x would give −40−40 streamers.
Key idea
The five steps. First, name what the letter stands for and write it down, so you never solve for the wrong thing. Second, translate the sentence into an equation one phrase at a time, by meaning rather than left to right. A phrase like seven less than the number is x−7x−7, not 7−x7−x. Third, solve with the tools you already have. Fourth, report the exact quantity the question asked for. Fifth, read your answer back into the original sentence to check it fits.
Problem
A workshop has two number machines. The first triples a secret number and subtracts 55, and its readout shows 4040. The second doubles that same number and adds 22. First solve for the secret number, then feed it into the second machine. What does the second machine's readout show?
Show a hint
  • Give the secret number a name, say nn. The first machine triples it and subtracts five to read forty, so that sentence becomes an equation in nn. Solve that equation first, then look again at what the question is actually asking for.
  • Solve 3n−5=403n−5=40 to find n=15n=15, but do not stop there. The question asks for the second machine's reading, which is 2n+22n+2. Put n=15n=15 into 2n+22n+2 and compute that number.
Show the full solution
Let nn be the secret number. The first machine triples it and subtracts five to show forty, so 3n−5=403n−5=40, giving 3n=453n=45 and n=15n=15. The question wants the second machine, which reads 2n+2=2⋅15+2=322n+2=2⋅15+2=32​. Solving for the variable is not always the last step. Check what the question actually asked for before you answer.
Problem
A rooftop garden has 9696 plants, all marigolds and lavender, with three times as many lavender as marigolds. Let mm be the number of marigolds, so the lavender count is 3m3m and the two add to 9696. The question asks for lavender, not mm. How many lavender plants are there?
Show a hint
  • Pick the smaller, simpler quantity to name with a variable. Let mm be the number of marigolds. Then write the lavender count in terms of mm, and remember the two kinds together make 9696 plants.
  • There are three times as many lavender as marigolds, so the lavender count is 3m3m. The total ties them together, so m+3m=96m+3m=96. Combine to get 4m=964m=96, solve for mm, then read the question again. It asks for lavender, which is 3m3m, not mm.
Show the full solution
Let mm be the marigolds, so the lavender count is 3m3m. The two kinds are the whole garden, so m+3m=96m+3m=96, which gives 4m=964m=96 and m=24m=24 marigolds. The question asks for lavender, which is 3⋅24=723⋅24=72​ plants. Check it. 24+72=9624+72=96, and 7272 is three times 2424.
Key idea
Solve for the letter, then answer the question. The letter you name is not always the quantity the question asks for. In the garden problem all the algebra was right and mm came out to 2424. But that was the marigold count, and the question asked for lavender, so the answer was 7272. Before you start, find the actual question and underline it. Once you have your number, check whether it is the quantity asked for, and if not, take the extra step to get there.
Problem
A 150150 cm ribbon is cut into two pieces, with the longer piece 3030 cm more than the shorter. Let xx be the shorter piece, so the longer is x+30x+30 and the two add to 150150. The question asks for the longer piece, not xx. How long is the longer piece, in centimeters?
Show a hint
  • You have two unknown lengths, but you do not need two letters. Let xx stand for the shorter piece. Since the longer piece is 3030 more than the shorter one, you can write it as x+30x+30. Now both pieces are written with the same single letter.
  • The two pieces together make the whole 150150 centimeter ribbon, so x+(x+30)=150x+(x+30)=150. Combine to get 2x+30=1502x+30=150, then 2x=1202x=120, so x=60x=60. That is the shorter piece. The question asks for the longer piece, which is x+30x+30.
Show the full solution
Let xx be the shorter piece in centimeters, so the longer piece is x+30x+30. The two came from one ribbon, so x+(x+30)=150x+(x+30)=150, which is 2x+30=1502x+30=150, then 2x=1202x=120 and x=60x=60. The question asks for the longer piece, x+30=90x+30=90​ centimeters. Writing the second length in terms of the first keeps the whole problem on one variable.
Key idea
One letter can cover every unknown. When two unknown amounts add to a total you already know, you do not need two letters. Call one of them xx, and since the pieces must add to the total, the other is the total minus xx. Runs of consecutive numbers work the same way. Let the first be nn and write the rest as n+1n+1, n+2n+2, stepping by 22 instead for consecutive even or odd numbers. A problem with several unknowns then becomes an ordinary one-variable equation.

That dictionary is the whole vocabulary. Every word problem is built from those same few phrases, so no new translation rules are coming. What changes is how many phrases stack into one story and which quantity the question finally asks for. The next problems run on the same five steps in fuller settings, including counts of two different kinds of thing, a choice between two pricing plans, ages a few years apart, and runs of consecutive whole numbers.

Problem
A puzzle box holds 3030 tokens, each a square with 44 corners or a triangle with 33 corners, and all the corners together count 104104. Let ss be the number of squares, so the triangles are 30−s30−s, the key move being that the second category is the total minus the first. The question asks for triangles. How many triangle tokens are in the box?
Show a hint
  • You know two totals here, the number of tokens and the number of corners. Pick a letter for one of the counts. Let ss be the number of squares. Since the two kinds add up to 3030 tokens, how can you write the number of triangles using ss? Then total the corners, 44 for each square and 33 for each triangle.
  • The triangles must be 30−s30−s, the total minus the squares. Counting corners gives 4s+3(30−s)=1044s+3(30−s)=104. Distribute and combine like terms to get s+90=104s+90=104, so s=14s=14. That is the number of squares, so finish by computing the triangles the question wants, which is 30−1430−14.
Show the full solution
Let ss be the squares, so the triangles are 30−s30−s. Counting corners gives 4s+3(30−s)=1044s+3(30−s)=104. Distribute to get 4s+90−3s=1044s+90−3s=104, so s+90=104s+90=104 and s=14s=14 squares. The triangles are 30−14=1630−14=16​. Check it. 14+16=3014+16=30 tokens, and 4×14+3×16=1044×14+3×16=104 corners.
Problem
A street magician's riddle gives two descriptions of the same spot. Half her secret number with four shaved off lands exactly where a third of her number with three piled on lands, so 12x−4=13x+321​x−4=31​x+3. Clear the fractions, gather the variable, and solve. What is her secret number?
Show a hint
  • Let xx stand for the secret number. Now translate each half of the sentence on its own. "Half of my number and shave off four" becomes 12x−421​x−4, and "a third of my number and pile on three" becomes 13x+331​x+3. The phrase "land in exactly the same spot" is the equals sign, so set the two pieces equal.
  • You have 12x−4=13x+321​x−4=31​x+3, with the variable on both sides and fractions in the way. Clear the fractions by multiplying every single term by 66. That turns it into 3x−24=2x+183x−24=2x+18. Now gather the xx terms on one side and the numbers on the other, and solve.
Show the full solution
Both descriptions land on the same spot, so 12x−4=13x+321​x−4=31​x+3. Multiply every term by 66 to clear the fractions, giving 3x−24=2x+183x−24=2x+18. Subtract 2x2x, then add 2424, so her secret number is 4242​. Check it. Half of 4242 minus four is 1717, and a third of 4242 plus three is 1717 too.
Key idea
The variable on both sides. When a sentence mentions the number on both sides of the word equals, the equation you get has the variable on both sides. That is the kind you solved in 6.3, so gather the variable terms and finish. Fractions of the number work the same way. Multiply every term by a common multiple to clear the denominators first, then gather.
Problem
A climbing gym offers two plans. The Steady plan charges a flat $12$12 per month plus $0.20$0.20 per session, and the Casual plan charges a flat $4$4 per month plus $0.30$0.30 per session. For few sessions Casual is cheaper, for many Steady wins, so somewhere they cost the same. How many sessions in one month make the two plans cost the same amount?
Show a hint
  • Give the unknown a name. Let ss be the number of sessions in the month. Now write the monthly cost of each plan as an expression in ss, and remember that "cost the same" is just an equals sign waiting to happen. To keep everything in whole numbers you can work in cents, so $0.20$0.20 is 2020 cents and the flat $12$12 is 12001200 cents.
  • In cents the Steady plan costs 1200+20s1200+20s and the Casual plan costs 400+30s400+30s. Set them equal to get 1200+20s=400+30s1200+20s=400+30s. Get the variable on one side by subtracting 20s20s from both sides, then subtract 400400 from both sides, and finish by dividing.
Show the full solution
Let ss be the sessions in the month, and work in cents to stay exact. Steady costs 1200+20s1200+20s and Casual costs 400+30s400+30s, so they match when 1200+20s=400+30s1200+20s=400+30s. Subtract 20s20s to get 1200=400+10s1200=400+10s, then 800=10s800=10s, so the plans tie at 8080​ sessions. At 8080 sessions both come to 28002800 cents, which is $28$28.
Problem
Marisol notices that six years from now her tortoise Pebble will be exactly seven sixths of its current age. Let tt be Pebble's age now, so its future age is t+6t+6, and that equals 76t67​t. Clear the fraction and solve. How old is Pebble right now, in years?
Show a hint
  • Pick a letter for the thing you do not know yet, the age right now, and call it tt. A future age is just the current age plus however many years pass, so in six years Pebble will be t+6t+6. The words say that future age equals seven sixths of the age now, so set t+6t+6 equal to 76t67​t.
  • Start from t+6=76tt+6=67​t. The fraction is annoying, so multiply every single term by 66 to clear it, which gives 6t+36=7t6t+36=7t. Now it is an ordinary equation with the variable on both sides, so subtract 6t6t from each side and read off tt.
Show the full solution
Let tt be Pebble's age now. Six years from now the age is t+6t+6, and that equals 76t67​t, so t+6=76tt+6=67​t. Multiply every term by 66 to get 6t+36=7t6t+36=7t, then subtract 6t6t, so Pebble is 3636​ years old. Check it. 36+6=4236+6=42, and 76⋅36=4267​⋅36=42.
Fun fact
About 4,000 years ago Egyptian scribes posed "aha" puzzles that ask you to find the heap such that the heap plus a fraction of itself equals a total. All in words, no symbols, yet the logic is exactly this.
Problem
Three steel rings have weights that are consecutive even numbers of kilograms and total 9696 kg. What does the heaviest ring weigh, in kilograms?
Show a hint
  • Let nn stand for the weight of the lightest ring in kilograms. Because the rings step up by 22 each time, the middle ring is n+2n+2 and the heaviest is n+4n+4. The three weights add to 9696, so write that sum as an equation in nn.
  • Your equation is n+(n+2)+(n+4)=96n+(n+2)+(n+4)=96. Combine the like terms on the left to get 3n+6=963n+6=96, then subtract 66 and divide by 33 to find nn. Once you have nn, the question wants the heaviest ring, which is n+4n+4, not nn itself.
Show the full solution
Let nn be the lightest ring in kilograms. Consecutive even weights step up by 22, so the three rings are nn, n+2n+2, and n+4n+4, and they total 9696. That gives 3n+6=963n+6=96, so 3n=903n=90 and n=30n=30. The weights are 3030, 3232, and 3434, so the heaviest ring is 3434​ kilograms. The variable landed on the lightest ring, but the question wanted the heaviest, so take the extra step.
Problem
A baker fills exactly 4040 boxes, each a small box holding 66 cupcakes or a large box holding 1010, for a total of 312312 cupcakes. Let ss be the small boxes, so the large boxes are 40−s40−s. Count the cupcakes, solve, then answer for the large boxes. How many large boxes did she fill?
Show a hint
  • You have two unknowns but they are tied together. Let ss be the number of small boxes. Since every box is small or large and there are 4040 boxes in total, the number of large boxes must be 40−s40−s. Now count cupcakes, the small boxes contribute 6s6s and the large boxes contribute 1010 of them each.
  • Write the cupcake count as one equation, 6s+10(40−s)=3126s+10(40−s)=312. Distribute and combine like terms to get −4s+400=312−4s+400=312. Solve for ss, then remember the question asks for large boxes, which is 40−s40−s, not ss itself.
Show the full solution
Let ss be the small boxes, so the large boxes are 40−s40−s. Counting cupcakes gives 6s+10(40−s)=3126s+10(40−s)=312. Distribute to get 6s+400−10s=3126s+400−10s=312, so −4s+400=312−4s+400=312, then −4s=−88−4s=−88 and s=22s=22 small boxes. The large boxes are 40−22=1840−22=18​. Check it. 22+18=4022+18=40 boxes, and 6⋅22+10⋅18=3126⋅22+10⋅18=312 cupcakes.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A magician guessing the number on your card says, four more than triple your number lands exactly on thirty-one. What number is on the card?
Show the solution
Let xx be the number on the card. Triple it and add four to land on thirty-one, so 3x+4=313x+4=31. Subtract 4 from both sides for 3x=273x=27, then divide by 3, so the card reads 99​. Four more than triple means the tripling happens first and the four gets added after.
Practice
A lighthouse keeper logs ships each night. Wednesday's count was eight less than Tuesday's and came to 2323, and eight less than Tuesday's number is x−8x−8. How many ships passed on Tuesday?
Show the solution
Let xx be Tuesday's count. Eight less than that number is x−8x−8, and it came to 23, so x−8=23x−8=23. Add 8 to both sides, so 3131​ ships passed on Tuesday. Less than flips the order you hear. It is x−8x−8, never 8−x8−x.
Practice
A museum desk starts the morning with 5050 maps and 1212 remain by lunch. The number handed out subtracted from 5050 leaves 1212. How many maps were handed out?
Show the solution
Let xx be the maps handed out. They came off the pile of fifty and twelve remain, so 50−x=1250−x=12. Add xx and subtract 1212 from both sides to get 50−12=x50−12=x, so the desk handed out 3838​ maps. Subtracted from fifty puts the fifty first, so it is 50−x50−x and not x−50x−50.
Practice
Doubling the count of new birdhouses and adding 77 gives 3333. Solve for the count, then find how many would remain if five were taken down. How many birdhouses would be left?
Show the solution
Let xx be the birdhouses the crew hung. Doubling and adding seven gives 2x+7=332x+7=33, so 2x=262x=26 and x=13x=13. Taking five down leaves 13−5=813−5=8​ birdhouses. The variable was the number hung, not the number left, so that last subtraction is part of the answer.
Practice
Two bakery trays hold 4545 croissants together, and the window tray holds 99 fewer than the kitchen tray. How many croissants are on the kitchen tray?
Show the solution
Let kk be the croissants on the kitchen tray, so the window tray holds k−9k−9. The two trays hold 45 together, so k+(k−9)=45k+(k−9)=45. That is 2k−9=452k−9=45, so 2k=542k=54 and the kitchen tray has 2727​. Check it. The window tray has 27−9=1827−9=18, and 27+18=4527+18=45.
Practice
A llama drinks four times as much water as a goat, and together they drink 4040 liters. How many liters did the llama drink?
Show the solution
Let gg be the goat's liters, so the llama drank 4g4g. Together that is g+4g=40g+4g=40, so 5g=405g=40 and g=8g=8. The question asks about the llama, which is 4×8=324×8=32​ liters. Check it. 8+32=408+32=40, and 3232 is four times 88.
Practice
A robotics club builds 2626 machines, each a roller with 44 wheels or a hopper with 22 wheels, totaling 8484 wheels. How many hoppers did they build?
Show the solution
Let cc be the rollers, so the hoppers are 26−c26−c. Counting wheels gives 4c+2(26−c)=844c+2(26−c)=84, which expands to 4c+52−2c=844c+52−2c=84, so 2c+52=842c+52=84 and c=16c=16. The hoppers are 26−16=1026−16=10​. Check it. 16+10=2616+10=26 machines, and 4×16+2×10=844×16+2×10=84 wheels.
Practice
A satellite finds that a quarter of the ice crystal count plus 55 equals a sixth of the count plus 99. How many ice crystals are in the cloud?
Show the solution
Let xx be the ice crystals. A quarter of the count plus five equals a sixth plus nine, so 14x+5=16x+941​x+5=61​x+9. Multiply every term by 1212 to clear the fractions, giving 3x+60=2x+1083x+60=2x+108. Subtract 2x2x, then subtract 6060, so x=48x=48​. Check it. Both sides come out to 1717.
Practice
A club buys 1212 glow items, each a stick at $3$3 or a lantern at $5$5, spending $44$44 in all. How many glow lanterns did they buy?
Show the solution
Let pp be the glow sticks, so the lanterns are 12−p12−p. The spending gives 3p+5(12−p)=443p+5(12−p)=44, which expands to 3p+60−5p=443p+60−5p=44, so −2p+60=44−2p+60=44, then −2p=−16−2p=−16 and p=8p=8. The lanterns are 12−8=412−8=4​. Check it. 8+4=128+4=12 items, and 3⋅8+5⋅4=443⋅8+5⋅4=44 dollars.
Practice
Four years ago a boat was two thirds of its current age, so with tt its age now, t−4=23tt−4=32​t. How old is the boat now, in years?
Show the solution
Let tt be the boat's age now. Four years ago it was t−4t−4, which equals two thirds of its current age, so t−4=23tt−4=32​t. Multiply every term by 33 for 3t−12=2t3t−12=2t, then subtract 2t2t, so the boat is 1212​ years old. Check it. Four years ago it was 88, and 23×12=832​×12=8.
Practice
Priya and Dev's ages add to 4444 years, and Priya is exactly three times as old as Dev. How old is Priya, in years?
Show the solution
Let yy be Dev's age, so Priya's age is 3y3y. Their ages add to 4444, so y+3y=44y+3y=44, giving 4y=444y=44 and y=11y=11. The question asks for Priya, whose age is 3⋅11=333⋅11=33​ years. Check it. 11+33=4411+33=44, and 3333 is three times 1111.
Practice
Three hallway panels have consecutive integer widths in tiles that sum to 7272. How many tiles wide is the widest panel?
Show the solution
Let nn be the narrowest panel in tiles, so the three widths are nn, n+1n+1, and n+2n+2. They sum to 72, so 3n+3=723n+3=72, giving 3n=693n=69 and n=23n=23. The widths are 23, 24, and 25, so the widest panel is 2525​ tiles. Solving gives you the narrowest panel, so take one more step to reach the widest.
Practice
Two padlock codes are consecutive odd numbers that sum to 5656. What is the larger of the two codes?
Show the solution
Let nn be the smaller code. Consecutive odd numbers sit two apart, so the larger is n+2n+2 and n+(n+2)=56n+(n+2)=56. That is 2n+2=562n+2=56, so 2n=542n=54 and n=27n=27. The larger code is 27+2=2927+2=29​. Check it. 2727 and 2929 are both odd and add to 5656.
Practice
Garage A charges $5$5 plus $2$2 per hour, and Garage B charges $11$11 plus $1$1 per hour. At how many hours of parking do the two garages cost the same?
Show the solution
Let hh be the hours parked. Garage A costs 5+2h5+2h dollars and Garage B costs 11+h11+h, and they charge the same when 5+2h=11+h5+2h=11+h. Subtract hh for 5+h=115+h=11, then subtract 55, so the costs match at 66​ hours. At 66 hours both garages come to $17$17.

Learn it by doing it

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
